security_fix_forward.trigger: BLOCKING adversarial-skeptic finding after the base T-0633 review approved: vertical privilege escalation via the preferred_username → employee.slug identity fallback (resolveActorSlugFromAuth, src/db/org.ts).
security_fix_forward.vector: The fallback's prior security comment claimed 'Keycloak username uniqueness makes a seeded-persona slug un-mintable' — FALSE for kind='human' seed personas that lack a KC user at install: genesis 'e-owner' (migrations/026: tenant-owner + 16 delegable mgmt_object grants = cross-tenant super-admin) and 'e-configurator' (migrations/088). Neither is in config/keycloak/realm-choros.json, so KC does NOT 409 on username='e-owner'. A holder of mgmt_object:employee:create (POST /api/users, NOT the owner) could mint a KC user login='e-owner', log in, and be resolved to the forest-owner via the fallback. T-0633's own change widened the blast radius by wiring this resolver onto app-secret/llm-connections/etc. where the fallback was previously unreachable.

fix_approach.anti_collision: POST /api/users (src/http/user-mgmt.ts) and self-registration (src/core/register.ts, defense-in-depth) REJECT with 409 LOGIN_RESERVED — BEFORE any Keycloak call, no side-effect — any login/username colliding with an existing kind='human' employee.slug in ANY tenant. Backed by ONE canonical cross-tenant existence query, humanEmployeeSlugExists(pool, slug), newly exported from src/db/org.ts and shared by BOTH the guard and the resolver (extracted from the resolver's former inner helper — single source, cannot drift).
fix_approach.fallback_narrowing_decision: NOT narrowed — deliberate. The legitimate genesis-owner login depends on exactly this preferred_username → slug fallback (its KC sub is a random UUID ≠ its slug 'e-owner'; KC user provisioned out-of-band). The resolver cannot distinguish a genuine token from a forged one with the same preferred_username, so any resolver-level narrowing that blocked a forged 'e-owner' would also block the genuine owner. Vector cut at mint instead. All four narrowing options (tenant-scope, allow-list, UUID-shape, fallback-removal) evaluated and rejected in T-0633.adr.md::security_fix_decision.rejected_alternatives.
fix_approach.kc_provision_note: e-owner/e-configurator KC users are not seeded by migrations and now not mintable via any product route (both 409). They must be provisioned deliberately out-of-band at install (already the stand's reality — memory/choros-acceptance-t0583-users-2026-07-04). FOLLOW-UP (out of scope, non-blocking): a genesis-installer step or migration that binds these seed personas to a stable KC identity so the manual step is captured.

security_fix_forward.legit_owner_login_preserved: YES — verified two ways: (1) unit test resolve-actor-slug.test.ts (g) proves a token with sub=random-UUID (miss) + preferred_username='e-owner' STILL resolves to 'e-owner' (the fallback is untouched); (2) the fallback code path and its kind='human' guard are byte-unchanged except for the comment rewrite and the delegation to the extracted (identical-SQL) humanEmployeeSlugExistsOnClient — no behavioral change to resolution, only the mint side is newly guarded.

summary: T-0633: recurrence of T-0371's identity-resolution bug in 9 route modules (agents-list.ts, llm-connections.ts, llm-config.ts, llm-connection-test.ts, spend.ts, grant-trail.ts, process-catalog.ts, app-secret.ts, pdp-explain.ts) plus one inline block (src/http/org.ts's GET /api/org handler). Each had a local, synchronous `extractActor(req): string` helper (or, in pdp-explain.ts, `extractCaller`; in org.ts, an inline block) that returned the RAW keycloak JWT `sub` in keycloak mode instead of resolving it to the real employee slug. Since employee.slug != KC sub for any seeded persona (including the genesis-owner), resolveActorTenant (keyed on employee.slug) could not find a matching row and threw HttpError(403, ACTOR_TENANT_UNRESOLVED) even for the legitimate tenant owner — hiding Agents, LLM connections, org structure, PDP-explain, spend, grant-trail, and the process catalog behind a false 403 for every keycloak-mode seeded persona. Fixed by mirroring the CANONICAL pattern already correct in src/http/agents.ts::extractActor (and org.ts's own /api/my-tenant + /api/me/nav-capabilities in the SAME file): each fixed extractActor/extractCaller/inline-block became async, took the route's pool, and called resolveActorSlugFromAuth(pool, ctx.sub, ctx.preferredUsername) (sub-first, preferred_username fallback, T-0371's canonical resolver, src/db/org.ts) — a null result now throws 401 UNAUTHENTICATED instead of silently falling through to an unresolvable UUID. dev mode (x-dev-user) is completely unchanged in every file. No authz predicate (canConfigureLlmConnection, loadAdminContext/holdsAgentMgmtUpdate, checkExplainAuthz) was touched — only the identity feeding into them was corrected, so a non-owner/no-grant caller still gets an honest 403 BY RIGHT (a specific authz code), never a free pass.
routes_fixed: POST /api/pdp/explain (src/http/pdp-explain.ts — narrower manifestation: tenantId is pinned to DEV_TENANT_ID regardless of actor per this route's Day-1 design, so the bug surfaced as a wrong `caller` value feeding the self-query check and loadAdminContext's actor key, not as ACTOR_TENANT_UNRESOLVED)
GET /api/org (src/http/org.ts — bug was inlined in the GET /api/org handler only; /api/my-tenant and /api/me/nav-capabilities in the same file were already correct)
resolver_used: resolveActorSlugFromAuth(pool, sub, preferredUsername) — src/db/org.ts:450-503, the canonical T-0371 resolver. Contract: (1) sub-first — if an employee with slug===sub (kind='human') exists, return sub (short-circuits for self-registered users, T-0342 invariant); (2) else if an employee with slug===preferredUsername (kind='human') exists and preferredUsername!==sub, return preferredUsername (the seeded-persona fallback); (3) else null (fail-closed — the caller must throw 401, never fall through to an unresolvable UUID). Not modified by this task — reused as-is in every fixed file, mirroring src/http/agents.ts's existing extractActor.
